title: Tax is calculated on the undiscounted subtotal, so orders of 1,000.00 or more are overcharged
summary: Tax is 10% of the subtotal before the 5% discount instead of 10% of the discounted subtotal. Every discounted order total is too high by 0.5% of the subtotal.
steps: Sign in as acme-1 over the API
POST /api/orders with 80 x p-102 (1,250 each): subtotal 100000, discount 5000 (see evidence/api/undefined-B3.json)
Observe tax_cents 10000 and total_cents 105000
Repeat with 12 x p-107 (evidence/api/undefined-B4.json): tax 10799, total 113388
UI: Client Portal > New order, reference QA-ui-1, Printer Toner Cartridge x 12, Place order: confirmation says Total $1,133.88
expected: Tax = 10% of (subtotal - discount): 9500 / total 104500 for the first case; 10259 / 112848 for the second ($1,128.48 on screen)
actual: Tax 10000 and total 105000; tax 10799 and total 113388 ($1,133.88 on screen). Below 1,000.00 totals are correct (987.50 case matched).
suspected_cause: src/pricing.mjs computes tax from subtotal rather than subtotal - discount

regression_test.description: Price an order at exactly 100000 cents subtotal and expect tax 9500 and total 104500

plain.title: Customers are charged too much tax on large orders
plain.where: Client Portal → New order → order confirmation, and every order page
plain.what_happens: Orders of $1,000 or more get the 5% discount, but tax is still worked out on the full price. An order of $1,079.88 shows a total of $1,133.88 instead of $1,128.48.
plain.who_is_affected: Every customer placing an order of $1,000 or more, and staff reading sales totals.
how_to_see_it: Sign in to the Client Portal as a customer
Type a reference starting with QA-
Choose Printer Toner Cartridge and set Quantity to 12
You see a total of $1,133.88; the correct total is $1,128.48
plain.expected: Tax is worked out after the discount is taken off.

title: Order quantities are not checked: 0, negative, decimals, above 1,000 and empty orders are accepted
summary: POST /api/orders accepts quantity 0, -3, 1.5 and 1001, and an empty items list. A negative quantity produces a negative total.
steps: Sign in as acme-1 over the API
POST /api/orders with quantity -3 (evidence/api/undefined-Q-1.json) and observe 201
Repeat with 0, 1.5, 1001 and items [] (other evidence files)
expected: 400 naming the field: whole number 1 to 1000, at least one item
actual: 201 for every one of these; order created
suspected_cause: validateOrderInput only checks that quantity is a number and does not check range, integer or non-empty items

regression_test.description: POST orders with quantity 0, -3, 1.5, 1001 and empty items; expect 400 each

plain.title: The system accepts orders with impossible quantities
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal)
plain.what_happens: An order can be placed for zero, negative, fractional or more than 1,000 items, or for no items at all. A negative quantity gives a negative total that reduces sales figures.
plain.who_is_affected: The company's sales figures and anyone relying on order totals.
plain.expected: Orders are refused unless every quantity is a whole number from 1 to 1,000 and there is at least one item.

title: A customer can open another company's order by its address
summary: GET /api/orders/{id} returns any order to any signed-in client without checking the company.
steps: Sign in as acme-1, POST /api/orders with reference QA-iso-1 and note the id
Sign in as bright-1 (a different company) and GET /api/orders/<that id>
Observe 200 with the order body (evidence/api/undefined-I2.json)
actual: 200 with the other company's order including its reference
suspected_cause: getOrder looks up the order by id only, with no client_id comparison (the list endpoint does filter)

regression_test.description: Client B requests client A's order id and expects 403 or 404

plain.title: One company's customer can read another company's order
plain.where: Client Portal → an order page (the address ends in the order number)
plain.what_happens: Anyone signed in as a customer can open any other company's order by changing the number in the address, and see its contents and prices.
plain.who_is_affected: Customers of every company; their orders are not private.
plain.expected: Company B is refused and sees nothing of Company A's order.

title: Customers can read the admin customer list
summary: GET /api/admin/customers returns 200 to client accounts; only admins should see customers.
steps: Sign in as bright-1 over the API
GET /api/admin/customers
Observe 200 with customer records (evidence/api/undefined-I6.json); the same for acme-1, acme-2 and zain-1 in the admin baseline role matrix
expected: 403 for clients (per business rules and spec)
actual: 200 with the full customer list of all companies
suspected_cause: The route has no roles: ['admin'] option

plain.title: Any customer can see the full list of customers
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal)
plain.what_happens: The list of all customer records, meant for staff only, can be fetched by any customer account. The Client Portal does not show a link to it, but the system answers anyway.
plain.who_is_affected: Every company on the platform; their details are exposed to other customers.
plain.expected: Customers are refused; only admins can see the list.

title: A signed-out session still works
summary: After POST /api/auth/logout returns 204, the same bearer token still gets 200 from /api/me and /api/orders.
steps: Sign in as zain-1 over the API
POST /api/auth/logout (204)
GET /api/me with the same token (evidence/api/undefined-A3.json) and GET /api/orders (undefined-A4.json)
Observe 200 for both
suspected_cause: logout only sets endedAt and authenticate() never checks endedAt or expiresAt

regression_test.description: Log out, then call /me with the same token and expect 401; also with an expired session

plain.title: Signing out does not actually end the session
plain.where: Client Portal and Admin Portal → Sign out
plain.what_happens: The Sign out button takes the person back to the sign-in page, but the old sign-in is still accepted by the system behind the screens. Anyone who has a copy of it keeps full access.
plain.who_is_affected: Every user, especially those on shared computers.
plain.expected: After signing out the old sign-in stops working at once.

title: Clients see an old order status in My Orders after an admin changes it
summary: After an admin moves an order to processing, the client's order list still shows placed while the order detail shows processing.
steps: Sign in to the Client Portal as acme-1 and open My orders (list is read)
Close the browser; sign in to the Admin Portal as admin, open order QA-ui-1, set New status to Processing, click Update status
Close the browser; sign in to the Client Portal as acme-1 and open My orders: row shows Placed
Open the order: Status shows Processing
API chain: undefined-S3.json shows the same stale list
expected: My orders shows Processing straight away
actual: List shows Placed (also after a reload, about 10 seconds later); detail shows Processing
suspected_cause: listClientOrders caches copies of orders for 10 minutes and a status change does not clear the cache (only creating an order does)

regression_test.description: Warm a client's list, change status as admin, re-read the list and expect the new status

plain.title: Customers see an out-of-date order status in their order list
plain.what_happens: After staff move an order forward, the customer's list keeps showing the old status for a long time, while the order's own page shows the new one. The two screens disagree.
plain.who_is_affected: Customers tracking their orders; they may think nothing has happened.
how_to_see_it: Sign in to the Client Portal as a customer and open My orders
In another browser sign in to the Admin Portal, open that order and change its status to Processing
Back in the Client Portal reload My orders: the order still shows Placed
Open the order: it shows Processing
plain.expected: The list shows the new status straight away.

title: Malformed requests return internal technical details including server file paths
summary: Malformed JSON to /api/auth/login or /api/orders returns 400 whose body includes a stack trace with server file paths.
steps: POST /api/auth/login with raw body {"broken": (evidence/api/client-baseline-P007.json)
Observe error.trace containing a stack and local file paths
Same on POST /api/orders (client-baseline-P048.json)
expected: A 400 with a short message only
actual: 400 body includes trace with file paths and function names
suspected_cause: Error serializer includes err.stack for invalid_json

regression_test.description: Send malformed JSON and assert the body has no 'trace' or file paths

plain.title: Some error replies reveal the system's internal details
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal)
plain.what_happens: If a badly formed request reaches the system, the reply includes internal technical details and the location of files on the server, which helps an attacker.
plain.who_is_affected: The company, if someone probes the system.
plain.expected: Only a short, plain error message is returned.

title: Order list fails with a server error for page_size=0 and for search text that is not a valid pattern; negative page_size is accepted
summary: GET /api/orders returns 500 for page_size=0 and for q=( or q=\ (q is used as a regular expression); page_size=-1 or -5 returns 200.
steps: Sign in as acme-1 over the API
GET /api/orders?page_size=0 (evidence client-baseline-P019.json): 500
GET /api/orders?q=( (P024) and q=\ (P028): 500
GET /api/orders?page_size=-5 (undefined-L3.json): 200 with page_size -5
expected: 400 for invalid page_size; search text treated literally
suspected_cause: page_size lower bound is not checked (Math.ceil(n/0) gives Infinity array length); q is passed to new RegExp()

regression_test.description: GET /orders with page_size=0, q='(' and expect 400 or 200, never 500

plain.title: Searching or paging orders in unusual ways makes the system fail
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal)
plain.what_happens: Typing a bracket or backslash into an order search, or asking for zero items per page, makes the system fail instead of answering normally.
plain.who_is_affected: Customers and staff who search orders using punctuation.
plain.expected: Search text is treated as plain text and bad page sizes are refused politely.

title: Sending the same order twice at once creates two orders
summary: Two identical simultaneous POST /api/orders both return 201 and create separate orders. The spec does not document duplicates as intended; uncertain whether product wants protection.
steps: Sign in as acme-1 over the API
Send the same POST /api/orders body twice in parallel (evidence/api/client-baseline-P049.json)
Observe two 201 responses with different ids
expected: One order, or the second refused (no duplicate-protection is documented, so this is a judgment call)
actual: Two orders with the same reference
suspected_cause: No idempotency key or duplicate reference check; order creation also has 800 ms latency, which invites double clicks

regression_test.description: Submit the same order twice in parallel and assert only one is created

plain.title: Double-clicking Place order may create the same order twice
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal)
plain.what_happens: When the same order is sent twice at nearly the same moment, the system accepts both and creates two orders.
plain.who_is_affected: Customers who click twice or have a slow connection.

title: My orders on a phone: first order row is hidden under the toolbar and the Total column is cut off
summary: At 390 px the table's header and first row are covered by the status filter/New order toolbar, and the Total column is clipped inside a sideways-scrolling box with no hint.
steps: Sign in to Client Portal as acme-1 at width 390x844
Open My orders
Audit shows covered elements (first row under toolbar); table scrollWidth 452 vs 359 wide; totals cut off (screenshots/client-my-orders-mobile.png)
expected: No overlap; all columns reachable or stacked
actual: Row overlapped and totals show as '$1,133.' / '$7'
suspected_cause: Toolbar overlaps the table wrapper and the table has a fixed minimum width

regression_test.description: At 390 px viewport the order totals are fully visible and no element overlaps

plain.title: On a phone the order list is partly hidden and totals are cut off
plain.what_happens: On a narrow screen the first order is covered by the filter bar and the Total amounts are cut off at the screen edge with no sign that you can scroll.
how_to_see_it: Open the Client Portal on a phone (or a window about 390 pixels wide) and sign in as a customer
You see the first order partly hidden and totals cut off
plain.expected: All orders and totals are fully visible.
